records.reason: High-ratio hydrophobic aromatic control for constraining solvent interpolation and preventing carbonyl-tail corrections from shifting the neutral baseline.
Low-ratio dibromobenzaldehyde baseline tests whether aldehyde delay requires stronger solvent or is already present in weak conditions, complementing 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a and e8185e062559aff5c99e.
Simple acrylate ester control anchors ordinary ester behavior against the delayed multiacceptor rows 1a55639d058c08a1a06e and 20acd2ae49790ab82053.
High-loading hydroxy ester has a broad model endpoint interval and tests whether donor-capable ester chemistry develops a loading-sensitive V2 tail.
Large neutral polyaromatic control samples high-ratio retention with little silica functionality, protecting the common baseline during tail repair.
Halogenated nonpolar control at 1/1 DCM separates mass and hydrophobicity from the silica-interaction effects implicated by the polar failure families.
High-ratio aromatic ester probes whether broad V2 behavior extends beyond aldehydes and polycarbonyls, while retaining a single-carbonyl ester topology.
Intermediate-ratio neutral diester supplies a local multiester condition point for comparison with the broad V2 behavior of m80 and the loading-sensitive polyacceptor observations.
Acetophenone control at 1/1 PE anchors ordinary ketone response and limits transfer of the severe carbonyl corrections seen in 3fc05dc2025715e68174.
Bromomethyl aromatic ester probes a moderately polar ester topology at intermediate loading and ratio, filling a less extreme region between ordinary esters and delayed tails.
Weakly interacting fused aromatic control at 0/1 DCM constrains the low-strength neutral baseline and condition interpolation.
Diarylether-like neutral control at 0/1 PE tests whether donor-free oxygen alone causes late endpoints, separating generic heteroatom effects from nitrogen failures.
Low-ratio substituted acetophenone provides another ordinary ketone anchor for distinguishing scaffold-specific V2 tails from a general carbonyl correction.

Tertiary-amine acrylate at weak ratio tests whether basic nitrogen produces a distinct condition response from the fused nitrogen and amino-nitrile families represented by 49201b5817f204116f7f and a185774933bd6bb12c07.
Weak-ratio dibromo multiester baseline tests whether polyacceptor tails begin at low solvent strength or require a high-ratio threshold.
Matched m74 molecule and solvent at a different sample volume forms a direct loading contrast with 9807b8d6ea4e235596ef, helping separate loading from scaffold and solvent effects.
A donor-free, highly aromatic control with a wide model V2 interval tests whether broad endpoint predictions occur without strong silica hydrogen bonding.
Donor-containing neutral control at 1/1 DCM tests generic hydrogen bonding without nitrogen, providing a discriminator for the nitrogen-specific hypothesis.
Simple iodinated aromatic control at 2/1 DCM constrains heavy-atom and hydrophobicity effects in the ordinary retention regime.
Biphenyl aldehyde at 2/1 DCM tests whether aldehyde delay transfers to a more hydrophobic, donor-free scaffold before the high-ratio regime.
Halogenated ether control at 1/1 DCM helps distinguish heavy-atom and weak acceptor effects from the carbonyl and nitrogen failure families.
Quinoline at 1/1 PE supplies a fused ring-nitrogen control distinct from the severe pyridyl ketone observation 49201b5817f204116f7f and the ordinary m211 controls.
Higher-ratio m184 aldehyde extends the low-ratio m184 baseline and tests the solvent slope of a donor-free aldehyde with heavy halogens.
Ordinary diaryl ketone control at 2/1 DCM constrains carbonyl retention without multiple acceptors or donors.
High-ratio acrylate ester probes whether a single ester can develop the delayed finish seen in more strongly interacting carbonyl and polyacceptor scaffolds.
Alcohol-containing neutral control tests generic silica donor interactions and provides a comparison for the donor-bearing nitrogen rows.
Phenyl ketoester at 1/1 DCM samples an intermediate polycarbonyl regime between ordinary ketones and the delayed V2 observations 3fc05dc2025715e68174 and 20acd2ae49790ab82053.
High-ratio aromatic ester with a broad model V2 interval tests whether endpoint tails extend to polyaromatic ester topology rather than only aldehydes and beta-diketones.
Weak-ratio beta-diketone baseline helps identify whether the large V2 delays in 3fc05dc2025715e68174 and 20acd2ae49790ab82053 require stronger solvent.
A compact aryl cyclopropyl ketone at intermediate ratio tests ordinary ketone behavior in a less flexible scaffold and constrains universal carbonyl corrections.
Low-ratio fluoroalkyl acrylate provides an ordinary ester control with limited aromatic silica interaction, improving transfer across the common ester region.
Ordinary substituted benzaldehyde at 1/1 PE tests whether aldehyde tails are scaffold-specific, complementing the delayed aldehyde observations 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a and 654a4a40363a388cf9cb.

hypotheses.content: Donor-bearing basic molecules and fused or biaryl nitrogen heteroaromatics have scaffold-specific retention thresholds; a single nitrogen or polarity correction will not transfer across these topologies.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separate condition interactions for basic nitrogen, fused ring nitrogen, and donor-free heteroaromatics can prevent QGeoGNN from applying severe nitrogen residuals to ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do basic nitrogen and fused ring-N controls share a ratio slope after conditioning on loading, or do their V1 and V2 responses require separate interaction terms?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl, ester, aldehyde, and polyacceptor molecules develop delayed V2 tails only for particular scaffold and solvent combinations; a universal carbonyl-tail correction is unsafe.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The aldehyde, ester, beta-diketone, and ketoester controls teach endpoint-specific corrections while protecting ordinary ketone and ester predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which combinations of functional group, aromatic topology, and PE/EA ratio produce delayed finishes rather than ordinary bands?

hypotheses.content: Same-molecule condition responses can be nonlinear and endpoint-specific in nitrogen and polycarbonyl scaffolds, so local ratio, solvent, and loading contrasts are needed to distinguish condition response from scaffold residuals.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Condition bracketing gives the retrained model identifiable local slopes and thresholds instead of forcing transfer from unrelated structures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do local response curves become monotonic after separating loading amount from solvent strength, or do endpoint turnovers remain?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount can strongly change V2 in some silica-interacting or polyacceptor scaffolds, but the magnitude is conditional and weak in neutral controls.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched m74 points and high-loading polar controls can show whether loading should enter as a shared interaction or remain scaffold-specific.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched ratio and loading solvent, does increasing sample amount systematically widen V2 for polyacceptors while leaving neutral controls nearly unchanged?

hypotheses.content: Neutral hydrophobic, halogenated, ether, and simple ketone rows form a relatively stable common baseline across conditions, constraining repairs learned from rare late-regime failures.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ordinary controls reduce the risk that large corrections for polar and polycarbonyl failures degrade the common portion of the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can one shared neutral condition response explain the aromatic, ether, ester, and simple ketone controls across PE and DCM?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes reinforce conditional endpoint behavior. The m72 results 71f5df8c7d7e88d1afce, eb798a5ccfb1f429a724, and 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 vary strongly across conditions, while 1a55639d058c08a1a06e and 20acd2ae49790ab82053 separate V2 tail behavior from onset. Large errors remain concentrated in nitrogen-rich or heteroaromatic rows such as 49201b5817f204116f7f and d119d77f545c029deace, and in aldehyde or polycarbonyl scaffolds such as 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a and 3fc05dc2025715e68174. Neutral controls including e81cfc3293405e5d558f, 8f84fa7c65453783c74e, 31d2da0c82fdf1d7c27f, and d84e5afb325f6fd55103 were comparatively close, so this batch emphasizes conditional repair while retaining ordinary anchors. Loading outcomes aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58, aef5cafc63ca445e92fa, 4e66505f5d66d4fe37b9, and 7f3a3fa577dc73897305 continue to weaken any universal loading correction.
batch_rationale: The batch combines nitrogen and donor controls, aldehyde and polycarbonyl rows, matched m74 loading contrasts, and a broad set of ordinary hydrophobic, ether, ester, and ketone anchors. Weak and strong ratio points for related aldehydes and multiacceptors test whether delayed V2 tails have solvent thresholds. The m74 pair and high-loading donor-capable ester probe loading interactions, while neutral controls constrain the common baseline. This should improve generalization by teaching QGeoGNN which residuals are shared, which are endpoint-specific, and which depend on local scaffold-condition context.
